# A Bash guard refuses gh edit --body-file - fed by an unchecked pipe

## Context

A seat has twice blanked a GitHub body by piping a transform into `gh … edit --body-file -`:
- **2026-10-12, `neomjs/neo-stage#24`** (13k chars of a folded decision): the sed failed on an unescaped `/` and printed nothing.
- **2026-10-17 21:43Z, `neomjs/neo-stage#170`**, a PR under review: the node transform failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, because its path came from a glob that matched another session's scratch directory. The body sat at 0 chars for 33 s and was restored from GraphQL `userContentEdits`.

The same seat (Vega) had recorded the lesson after the first occurrence, and discipline did not hold. The defect-note at 21:45Z promotes it as a second occurrence.

## The Problem

A pipeline cannot keep the old value when its producer fails. `--body-file -` writes whatever arrives on stdin, and GitHub accepts an empty body for `pr edit` and `issue edit`. The producer doesn't matter (sed, node, jq). `set -o pipefail` alone doesn't help either: it only changes the exit code after the consumer has already written.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.claude/settings.json` runs two PreToolUse Bash guards: `.claude/hooks/rgReplaceGuardHook.mjs` (the `rg -r` footgun; it exports `tokenizeShellCommand`) and `.claude/hooks/harnessIdGuardHook.mjs`. Both fail open on a malformed payload.
- The spec precedent is `test/playwright/unit/hooks/rgReplaceGuardHook.spec.mjs`.

## The Fix

Add `.claude/hooks/bodyFileGuardHook.mjs` as a sibling that reuses `tokenizeShellCommand`, and register it in `.claude/settings.json` beside the rg guard.

It blocks a Bash command when a `gh pr edit` or `gh issue edit` segment reads its body from stdin (`--body-file -`, `--body-file=-`, `-F -`) and consumes a pipe. It allows the command if the producer is `printf` or `echo` of one variable and the command checks that variable's length or emptiness (`${#V}`, `-n "$V"`, `-z "$V"`).

The block message names the failure and the safe shape:
`set -o pipefail; V=$(producer) || exit 1; [ ${#V} -gt N ] || exit 1; printf '%s' "$V" | gh … edit --body-file -`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] It blocks `gh pr view 1 --json body --jq .body | sed s/a/b/ | gh pr edit 1 --body-file -`, and the same with a `node` or `jq` producer, `--body-file=-`, `-F -`, or `gh issue edit`.
- [ ] It allows the guarded variable shape above, `gh pr edit 1 --body-file body.md`, a heredoc body, and `gh pr create … --body-file -`, where an empty body loses nothing.
- [ ] It fails open on a malformed payload, as the rg guard does.
- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/hooks/bodyFileGuardHook.spec.mjs` covers each arm. Mutation: a guard that never sees the pipe lets the sed shape through and fails the spec.

## Out of Scope

- `gh api -X PATCH … -f body="$V"` with an unchecked variable: the same class, a second rule if it recurs.
- Other harness families' hook systems: the defect-note reached them.

## Related

- `neomjs/neo-stage#24`, `neomjs/neo-stage#170`: the two occurrences.

assignments and env no longer hide the consumer, and the shared tokenizer

reading unchanged."

[ -n $V ], which passes when V is empty, both admitted an empty body
(Euclid's round 2). The shared tokenizer now keeps a word's quotes when
asked, the check's operand and printf's value must be "$V", and command
words and keywords are still read as the shell reads them, so a quoted
"gh" stays a consumer."
